historical_growth.growth_rate_source: guidance-anchored, not a historical CAGR: FY2026-28 EBIT ex-nuclear outlook (9.2-10.2 -> 10.3-11.3bn) implies ~5% EBIT CAGR on ~2.5% nominal revenue growth; terminal 2.0% in base
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 2.6% vs revenue 5.2% and owner-FCF 16.1%: divergence >30%. Revenue is dominated by commodity pass-through (FY2022 EUR 93.9bn crisis peak, hence the -8.5% 3yr CAGR); EPS CAGRs are null because FY2020 EPS was negative (-0.71) and FY2022 was EUR 0.06 after impairments; the FCF CAGRs run from the Covid trough (FY2020 owner FCF 2,424) and the FY2022 base (2,115) to a NORMALIZED FY2025 (5,117) so they overstate underlying growth. None of these is used as the forward growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series used for CAGRs: reported FCF less IFRS 2 SBC (FY2020 2,474-50; FY2022 2,207-92; FY2025 normalized 5,228-111). Interest income is not inside Engie's OCF so no interest adjustment applies to the history.

scenario_narratives.base: Engie executes the 2026-28 plan roughly at the guidance midpoints: EBIT ex-nuclear rises from ~EUR 9.7bn (FY2026, UKPN from May) to ~EUR 10.8bn by FY2028 as French network tariffs (ATRD7, 5.87% gas-distribution equalization from July 2026), UKPN's full-year contribution and ~6 GW/yr of renewables/BESS additions outweigh the normalization of energy-management and gas-generation spreads. The EUR 34-38bn capex plan is charged in full, so owner FCF stays thin (EUR 2.3-3.6bn) through FY2029 while the RAB and contracted fleet grow, then widens to ~EUR 8bn by FY2035 as the build-out cadence normalizes relative to a larger revenue base. Leverage holds at or below the 4.0x economic net debt/EBITDA ceiling via EUR 4bn of disposals; no further equity. The axes that matter: (1) regulated-return resets in France and the UK, (2) the pace at which merchant/trading earnings normalize, (3) whether the growth capex earns the ~7% pre-tax return the margin path assumes, (4) Belgian nuclear provision outcomes, which sit in the bridge.
scenario_narratives.bull: Regulated mix shift pays off faster: UKPN accretive from year one, RIIO-ED3 (from April 2028) lands near ED2 returns, French CRE tariff periods hold allowed returns with higher rates, and data-centre PPAs (3-4 GW by 2030) plus LatAm transmission lift contracted EBITDA. Guidance is met at the top end (EBIT ex-nuclear EUR 11.3bn FY2028), the performance plan keeps delivering, DBSO and tax-equity recycling trims net capex from FY2028, and the market re-rates Engie toward network-peer multiples. Terminal 2.5% growth and a 24x FCF exit.
scenario_narratives.bear: Merchant and trading earnings keep normalizing below the plan (energy-management EBIT was already -52% organic in 2025), hydro/weather is unfavourable, and French and UK regulators reset allowed returns lower at ATRD7/RIIO-ED3 under household-bill pressure. UKPN integration and the EUR 4bn disposal programme slip, so leverage stays above 4x and the rating is pressured; growth capex earns weaker returns, leaving margins stuck ~21.5%. The ONDRAF/CPN dismantling-cost dispute is resolved against Engie, raising the provision deducted in the bridge. Terminal 1.5% growth, 20x exit.

valuation_philosophy.summary: House basis: unlevered owner FCF (SBC expensed, flat share count) on a NORMALIZED FY2025 base that strips the EUR 15.9bn Belgian nuclear payment from working capital, projected from components anchored to Engie's own FY2026-28 EBIT/EBITDA/capex guidance, discounted at a EUR-built 6.0% WACC. Every claim ahead of common is deducted once: net financial debt (incl. leases), nuclear/dismantling/pension provisions net of plan assets, hybrid notes at nominal, and NCI at book. Growth capex is charged in full in the explicit years with the matching EBITDA uplift, then faded so terminal reinvestment matches terminal growth; the terminal cap is set relative to the 6% Gordon value rather than the 10%-WACC house default, and no multiple expansion versus today's ~26x EV/normalized-FCF is assumed.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capex-return assumption: the EUR 34-38bn 2026-28 plan is charged in full; if it earns less than the ~7% pre-tax return embedded in the margin path (US renewables delays, grid-equipment inflation, regulatory disallowances) the value falls roughly EUR 1.5/share per 0.5pp of terminal margin
Terminal cap sensitivity: at 6% WACC the cap (18-24x) binds in every scenario; each 2x of cap is worth ~EUR 3-4/share
Leverage: net financial debt EUR 54.9bn and economic net debt EUR 60.3bn (4.2x EBITDA) against ~EUR 58bn market cap; a 50bp move in WACC is worth ~EUR 5/share
Regulatory resets (ATRD7 France, RIIO-ED3 UK from 2028) and political price intervention on B2C supply
Belgian nuclear: ONDRAF/CPN dismantling-cost revision could raise the EUR 5.4bn net provision bridge item; the 50/50 JV framework for Tihange 3/Doel 4 depends on Belgian policy stability
FX translation (GBP, BRL, USD) on ~40% of EBIT post-UKPN
The FY2025 FCF base is normalized by judgment; a reader using the as-filed EUR -8.7bn would reach a meaningless value

data_sources.financials: ENGI.PA_Metrics.csv (FY2015-FY2025, H1 FY2013-H1 FY2026) derived from the Universal Registration Documents and half-year reports; FY2025 URD cash flow statement and Notes 5.5/5.6/14.3; H1 FY2026 financial report Notes 2.1, 3.7, 3.8 and equity note (hybrids, share count); FY2025 and H1 FY2026 results presentations (guidance, capex plan, UKPN financing)

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 URD consolidated cash flow statement / Note 'Share-based payments (IFRS 2)' EUR 111m (FY2024 EUR 97m); no separate equity-award tax line (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 in kpis)
inputs.share_count_basis: 2,542,427,868 shares issued at 30 June 2026 (after the 107,142,857-share ABB at EUR 28 in Feb 2026 that part-funded UKPN) plus ~7m dilutive performance/bonus shares (FY2025 diluted average 2,443m vs basic ~2,436m) = 2,549m fully diluted; held FLAT because SBC (EUR 111m) is expensed in the flows. The 4.4% ABB is genuine non-SBC issuance and is already in the count.
inputs.fcf_basis: NORMALIZED FY2025 unlevered owner FCF, not the as-filed figure. As filed: OCF EUR -1,476m less capex EUR 7,267m = EUR -8,743m. The FY2025 'Change in working capital requirements' of EUR -13,986m contains the EUR 15,860m payment to the Belgian State for the nuclear waste/spent-fuel liability transfer (Note 5.5 CFFO reconciliation adds it back; the dedicated-fund assets that funded it came back through investing as +EUR 8,523m 'Change in loans and receivables'). Normalized: cash generated before tax and WC 13,525 - tax paid 1,016 + WC 0 (the residual +1,874 was mostly margin calls, treated as non-recurring) = 12,509 unlevered OCF; less gross PP&E/intangible capex 7,267 = 5,228 (reported_fcf); less SBC 111 = 5,117 owner FCF. Cross-check: company CFFO 13,641 + interest paid 1,512 - interest received 784 = 14,369 unlevered incl. the +1,874 WC inflow. Interest received is presented in investing/financing under Engie's IFRS election, so it is NOT inside OCF and no interest_income deduction is needed; the company is a net debtor in any case.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR flows discounted at a EUR-built WACC of 6.0%. CAPM: 10y OAT ~3.3-3.5%, beta ~0.75, ERP 5.5% -> cost of equity ~7.4%; pre-tax cost of debt 4.2% (reported average cost of gross financial debt, H1 FY2026), ~3.2% after tax. At market weights (equity ~EUR 58bn vs net financial debt + hybrids ~EUR 62bn) the CAPM build gives ~5.3%; at a 40/60 debt/equity target it gives ~5.7%. 6.0% is used as the single rate for all three scenarios (risk is charged in the flows, not stacked in the discount rate) and sits inside the 5.5-6.5% range used for large European multi-utilities. Regulated networks are ~half of EBIT post-UKPN; merchant generation, energy management, B2C supply and LatAm/BRL exposure are the reason not to go lower.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt. IFRS 16 lease liabilities (EUR 3,674m at FY2025) sit inside Engie's 'Borrowings and debt' and therefore inside the EUR 54,922m net financial debt used as net_debt. Lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows (it is in financing); ongoing lease-asset renewal is charged as ~0.4pp of revenue inside capex_pct_path (lease payments run ~EUR 0.6bn/yr; the existing liability turns over in ~8 years so a partial renewal charge avoids double-counting).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated; non-controlling interests (EUR 8,567m book at 30 June 2026 — Engie Brasil Energia 31.3% minority, Ocean Winds and other partnered renewables) are deducted once, in the equity_bridge, at book value. NRI attributable to NCI was EUR 467m in H1 FY2026 (~EUR 0.9-1.0bn annualized), so book (~9x) is a mid estimate between a listed-minority mark and an earnings multiple.
inputs.net_debt_note: net_debt = company-defined net financial debt EUR 54,922m at 30 June 2026 (Note 3.7), post-UKPN (UKPN added ~EUR 19bn incl. EUR 7bn assumed debt; offset by the EUR 3.0bn ABB and EUR 2.3bn hybrid). total_debt 69,425 = LT borrowings 55,188 + ST borrowings 14,237 (incl. leases); cash 13,537. total_debt - cash = 55,888 differs from net_debt by EUR 966m of derivative/other-financial-asset netting in the company's reconciliation; the company figure is used. Debt-like claims that are NOT in net financial debt are deducted in equity_bridge: nuclear/dismantling/pension provisions net of plan assets (EUR 5,353m = economic net debt 60,275 - net financial debt 54,922), hybrid deeply-subordinated perpetual notes EUR 6,693m nominal (equity-classified under IFRS, coupons paid out of equity, rank ahead of common), and NCI EUR 8,567m.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row 2: non-US operating company + adaptations). Engie is an integrated operating utility, not a REIT/LIC/bank: ~half of post-UKPN EBIT is regulated networks (GRTgaz/GRDF French RAB ~EUR 32bn, UKPN), the rest is renewables/BESS with PPAs, gas generation, energy management and retail supply. A RAB-based SOTP would be the alternative; the engine route was chosen because consolidated cash flows and the company's own 2026-28 EBIT/EBITDA/capex guidance are the cleaner anchors, with the regulated mix expressed through a utility WACC (6.0%), a margin path tied to guidance, and a terminal cap set against a 6% WACC (Gordon at 6%/2% is 25.5x FCF; cap 22x in base). Capex is the critical judgment: the EUR 34-38bn 2026-28 plan (~15-16% of revenue, ~2x D&A) is charged in full in the explicit years, with EBITDA margin lifted in step with guidance (EBIT ex-nuclear 9.2-10.2 / 9.8-10.8 / 10.3-11.3bn for FY26/27/28), then capex fades to ~11% by FY2034 so the terminal reinvestment rate is consistent with 2% growth; capitalizing peak build-out capex in perpetuity would value a growing RAB as if it never earned a return. Nuclear: Doel 1/2 and Tihange 1 closed in 2025; Tihange 3/Doel 4 are in a 50/50 equity-accounted JV with the Belgian State, so nuclear EBITDA is ~0 going forward and the projection is on an ex-nuclear basis; dismantling provisions are deducted in the bridge (the ONDRAF/CPN cost dispute is a bear-case risk to that bridge item, not modelled in the flows). SBC is EUR 111m (0.15% of revenue) so the house/street band is ~EUR 0.6/share wide; band_position is numerically valid but nearly degenerate. Buybacks (EUR 22m FY2025, EUR 175m H1 FY2026) are treasury purchases for employee plans, not a capital-return programme; the flat count is a modelling convention funded by SBC expensing. Price is a Friday regular close, not after-hours; no volatility flag.

bear.rationale: Bottom of FY2026 guidance (EBITDA ~14.3bn, 20.3%) and merchant normalization continues: Energy Management EBIT fell 52% organically in 2025 and captured spark spreads keep compressing; ATRD7 and RIIO-ED3 reset allowed returns lower; UKPN accretion slips; growth capex earns weaker returns (US renewables delays, grid-equipment inflation, disallowances) so margins plateau at 21.5%; capex follows the same fade as base because management has said it would trim growth capex if returns disappoint (charging full plan capex AND weak returns would charge the risk twice); recurring ETR at the top of the range (22%). Terminal 1.5% (structural French gas-volume decline) with a 20x cap (~88% of the 22.6x Gordon value at 6%/1.5%). Not in the flows but a live risk to the bridge: an upheld ONDRAF dismantling-cost increase would raise the EUR 5.4bn provision item.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 -1%: H1 revenue -3.6% on lower commodity prices, partly offset by UKPN consolidated from May (~EUR 1.1bn for 8 months). FY2027 +3.5%: UKPN full year (~EUR 2.6bn, +3.6%) on flat underlying. Then 2.5% nominal (inflation-indexed tariffs + RAB growth, LatAm transmission) fading to 2.0% from FY2032 as French gas-network volumes decline structurally.
base.margin_rationale: Anchored to guidance: FY2026 EBITDA ex-nuclear EUR 14.3-15.3bn (mid 14.8 on ~71.2bn revenue = 20.8%) and EBIT ex-nuclear 9.2-10.2bn; FY2027 EBIT 9.8-10.8 (mid 10.3 + D&A ~5.5 = 15.8bn, 21.4%); FY2028 EBIT 10.3-11.3 (mid 10.8 + D&A 5.7 = 16.5bn, 21.9%). Thereafter +0.3-0.5pp/yr as ~EUR 6bn/yr of net investment (capex less D&A) at ~7% pre-tax returns and the networks/renewables mix shift lift the margin to 24% by FY2034, then flat.
base.capex_rationale: 2026-28 plan EUR 34-38bn net growth + maintenance capex (~EUR 12bn/yr incl. UKPN ~EUR 1.3bn/yr, ~15-16% of revenue) vs FY2025 gross PP&E capex 7,267 and FY2024 9,385. FY2026 lower (UKPN only 8 months). From FY2029 fades to ~11% (vs D&A ~7.8%) so terminal net investment (~3.6% of revenue) is consistent with 2% growth on ~EUR 100bn+ invested capital. Includes ~0.4pp lease-asset renewal (treatment A).
base.tax_rationale: Unlevered cash tax on EBIT ramps 15% -> 20%. FY2025 cash tax paid was 1,016 on ~9.6bn EBIT (10.6%) and FY2024 9.9%, helped by the interest shield (which belongs in WACC, not here), equity-method income already taxed inside EBITDA, and timing. Company guides a recurring ETR of 18-22% on pre-tax income and 'a lower tax rate over the period'; 20% unlevered is the statutory-blend-less-credits level (France 25.8%, UK/Belgium 25%, Brazil 34%).
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 6.0%/2.0% = 25.5x FCF; cap 22x binds. Today's EV (~EUR 133bn incl. hybrids, NCI and provisions) is ~26x normalized FY2025 owner FCF and ~9x FY2026 EBITDA, so the 22x exit assumes no multiple expansion. The house default 20x cap is calibrated to ~10% WACC names; a regulated-heavy utility discounted at 6% needs a cap nearer its own Gordon value or the cap, not the business, sets the answer. Caps are set per scenario as a roughly constant ~85% haircut on each scenario's own Gordon multiple: bear 20x vs 22.6x (1.5% g), base 22x vs 25.5x (2.0% g), bull 24x vs 29.3x (2.5% g); WACC is identical across scenarios.

bull.rationale: Top of the FY2026-28 guidance ranges (EBITDA 15.3bn FY26; EBIT 10.8 / 11.3bn FY27/28), UKPN accretive from year one with RIIO-ED3 settled near ED2 returns, data-centre PPAs (3-4 GW by 2030) and LatAm transmission convert on schedule, DBSO sell-downs and US tax equity keep net capex lower from FY2028, performance plan continues at ~EUR 0.5bn/yr, recurring ETR at the low end (18%). Terminal 2.5% with a 24x cap (still below Gordon 29x at 6%/2.5%).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 22x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear up: economic net debt/EBITDA is 4.2x post-UKPN (ceiling 4.0x), the equity is exposed to two regulators resetting allowed returns in 2026-28, to French-state and EU price-intervention risk on household supply, and to an unresolved nuclear dismantling-cost dispute. Bull down: a regulated-heavy utility's upside is capped by the regulators, and the bull case needs UKPN accretion, top-of-range merchant results and lower net capex to coincide.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
